title: In this town, nobody locks their doors

lines.text: In this town, nobody locks their doors. *Ever*.
The baker leaves his shop open all night. Mrs. Lee's door doesn't even *have* a lock.
Except *us*. Our front door has *seven* locks.
The kids at school call our house the *prison*.
Every night, Dad checks every lock. *Twice*.
The room next to mine has been empty since I was four.
And Dad never drives on Highway *Nine*. Even when it's faster.
So one night, I decided to prove the locks were *stupid*.
I tiptoed downstairs, and found Dad, *asleep* in a chair, right in front of the door.
So I went up to the attic instead.
In an old box, I found a newspaper.
Boy, six, sleepwalks out of unlocked home, onto Highway *Nine*.
The boy in the picture looked *exactly* like me.
He was locking us *in*. So he would never lose another kid.
I sat down next to his chair, and fell asleep there too.
In the morning, he didn't say a word. He just handed me my own *key*.
In this town, nobody locks their doors. Except the people who learned *why*.
